key_insight: An AI safety monitor can look much more or less reliable depending on how its test attacks are generated and optimized. In a case study of a former production OpenAI monitor, measured false negative rates ranged from 0.5% to 20.8%.
problem_solved: Monitor evaluations use simulated attacks as stand-ins for dangerous real-world behavior, but the choice and optimization of those attacks can substantially change the apparent safety results.
method: Evaluate a former production OpenAI monitor on transcripts generated by attack policies.
Vary the attack-policy generation method and the degree of optimization.
Compare false negative rates: dangerous behavior that the monitor fails to flag.
impact: Practitioners should treat monitor scores as dependent on the attack-generation setup, not as fixed measures of safety. Testing across attack methods and optimization levels can reveal weaknesses that a single evaluation setup misses.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: attack policy → agent transcript → safety monitor → flagged or missed.

paper_title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
paper_authors: Charlie Griffin, Oliver Makins, Asa Cooper Stickland, Alessandro Abate, Yarin Gal
